query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing the powder‐pack boriding treatment to produce a denser, thicker, and more uniform MB/M2B boride surface layer will improve the resistance of boride‐based components to molten-aluminum corrosion in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based alloy components with conventionally formed or native boride layers that are not optimized for molten-aluminum exposure.
generation.intervention: Apply an optimized powder-pack boriding process with increased temperature and extended duration to enhance the growth kinetics of MB and M2B borides, thereby forming a more continuous, dense protective layer.
generation.conditions: Exposure to molten aluminum under typical hot-dip plating temperatures (e.g., around 700°C) and time durations encountered in industrial operations.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, dense, low-porosity boride (MB/M2B) surface layer that acts as a diffusion barrier to impede the penetration and dissolution effects of molten aluminum.
generation.mechanism: The thicker, uniform boride layer reduces the diffusion of aluminum into the component substrate. This enhanced barrier minimizes the chemical attack and dissolution of metal elements from the substrate into the molten aluminum bath.
generation.predicted_outcome: Components receiving the optimized boriding treatment will exhibit a lower mass loss and slower corrosion rate in molten aluminum compared to those with standard or no boriding, thereby extending their service life in hot-dip aluminum-plating environments.
generation.baseline: The corrosion performance (mass loss and microstructural degradation) of components with conventional boriding or untreated surfaces in molten-aluminum conditions.
generation.boundary: The protective effect is expected to hold under typical operational temperatures (around 700°C) and immersion times of hot-dip aluminum-plating. Extreme variations in temperature, aluminum composition, or unanticipated interactions with other plating bath constituents may compromise the effect.
generation.uncertainty: The exact optimal parameters (temperature and duration) for the boriding treatment and the long-term stability of the modified boride layer in dynamic molten-aluminum environments remain to be precisely determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of boride-based component samples: one set treated with conventional boriding parameters and another set treated with the optimized high-temperature/extended-duration boriding process. Subject both sets to prolonged exposure in molten aluminum under conditions simulating hot-dip plating. Periodically assess mass loss, surface morphology, and phase integrity using techniques such as SEM, EDS, and XRD.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized borided samples do not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in mass loss and a more intact, uniform boride layer compared to the conventionally treated samples under identical molten-aluminum exposure conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Effect of Boronizing on the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of CoCrFeNiMn High-Entropy Alloy

Abstract: AbstractThe CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloys were treated by powder-pack boriding to improve their surface hardness and wear resistance. The variation of boriding layer thickness with time and temperature was studied. Then, the frequency factor D0 and diffusion activation energy Q of element B in HEA are calculated to be 9.15 × 10−5 m2/s and 206.93 kJ/mol, respectively. The diffusion behavior of elements in the boronizing process was investigated and shows that the boride layer forms with the metal atoms diffusing outward and the diffusion layer forms with the B atoms diffusing inward by the Pt-labeling method. In addition, the surface microhardness of CoCrFeNiMn HEA was significantly improved to 23.8 ± 1.4 Gpa, and the friction coefficient was reduced from 0.86 to 0.48~0.61.Keywords: high entropy alloy, boronizing, growth kinetics, boronizing mechanism, wear resistance
